# Runs

Stop a run. Runs are known as processes in Maitento.

**Library:** [Maitento](index.md#maitento), for apps. More in [Runs and events](../../../concepts/runs-and-events.md).

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`ProcessKill`](#processkill) | Stops a run in your tenant: an app, interaction, sandbox (capsule) or code pipeline run. |

### ProcessKill

Stops a run in your tenant: an app, interaction, sandbox (capsule) or code pipeline run.

```c
void ProcessKill(guid processId, string processType)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `processId` | `guid` | The run's id. |
| `processType` | `string` | What kind of run it is: `App`, `Interaction`, `Capsule` or `CodePipeline`, in any case. |

It asks the run to stop and returns straight away; the run ends with status `Killed` soon after. To know it has stopped, wait for it with the matching call: [`AppProcessAwait`](apps.md#appprocessawait), [`InteractionAwait`](interactions.md#interactionawait), [`CapsuleAwait`](sandboxes.md#capsuleawait) or [`CodePipelineAwait`](code-pipelines.md#codepipelineawait).

It stops only the run you name. Stopping an app run doesn't stop the runs it started: stop those too, if you need to.

Fails with `Invalid kill request: Process is not running` when the run has already ended, so stopping a run that may finish at any moment (the rest of the runs, once [`InteractionAwaitAny`](interactions.md#interactionawaitany) returns, say) belongs in a `try`/`catch`. Also fails with `Invalid process type: …`, and `… process … not found` when your tenant has no such run.
